summary: `ldc`/`ldc_w`/`ldc2_w` of CONSTANT_MethodHandle (15), MethodType (16) and Dynamic (17) reported `ClassFormatError: Invalid class file`. They now report `UnsupportedOperationException: Unsupported class file feature: ldc of a …`, matching the shape PR #43 established for `invokedynamic`. Measured first: javac emits no such `ldc` (27,902 JDK classes / 1,252,714 ldc sites / zero), so the fixtures are synthetic and labelled as such. Gate-② returned request-changes: widening the ldc arms had removed an accidental backstop, so two genuinely corrupt condy files (tag 17 below major 55; a Dynamic naming an absent bootstrap method) answered 'unsupported' where OpenJDK 26 cannot read them at all. The -fix round adds the JVMS 4.4 tag-vs-class-file-version table to validate_class — measured to be four rows, not the one that was reported — and leaves one named band open.
changes: classfile/src/constant_pool.rs — three payload-free ConstantPoolReference variants + their from_constant_pool arms
classfile/src/opcode.rs — 0x12/0x13 accept all three; 0x14 accepts only Dynamic (JVMS 6.5 wide/narrow split)
jvm-bytecode/src/verifier.rs — one new arm returning UnsupportedFeature; the Invokedynamic line is untouched
test-data/src/ldc/make_ldc_fixtures.py + test-data/ldc/*.class — six synthetic fixtures (4 positive, 2 negative controls)
tests/test_class_format.rs — two tests, one per direction

classfile/src/validation.rs — constant_pool_tags_fit_the_class_file_version: tags 15/16/18 need major >= 51, tag 17 needs >= 55 (JVMS 4.4). No attribute parsing, so it does not collide with the BootstrapMethods round.

test-data/src/ldc/make_ldc_fixtures.py + 4 new fixtures — LdcTag13, LdcTag14 (the 'tags 13/14 cannot be constructed' claim was false), LdcDynamicOldMajor (the regression), LdcDynamicNoBSM (the band left open)
tests/test_class_format.rs — the version table locked across four rows including one real javac class, and the remaining band asserted as it behaves today
verification: before/after captured by running each fixture end to end through run_class, not by reading source
ground truth: OpenJDK 26.0.1 loads and runs all four positive fixtures; it rejects both negative controls
M1 remove the new verifier arm -> host abort at jvm-bytecode/src/interpreter.rs:1063 (unimplemented!) — the arm is load-bearing
M2 from_constant_pool back to None / M3 ldc arms back to the old set -> positives red
M4 let ldc2_w take a MethodType -> negative control red
M5 constant-pool tag switch made a pass-through -> red, but via the classfile unit test, NOT via the new end-to-end test
cargo test --all: 558/0/1 -> 560/0/1 (+2, zero regressions); DoD 6 commands rc=0
regression reproduced independently in an isolated worktree: before ab872b7 both fixtures were ClassFormatError, after 3304f752 both were UnsupportedOperationException; OpenJDK 26 rejects both
the defect was wider than the reported row: tags 15 and 16 at major 50 showed the same inversion, so the fix is a four-row table rather than a tag-17 special case
cost: 0 of OpenJDK 26's 27,902 classes violate the table — but every class in that corpus is major 69/70, so it cannot exercise the >= 51 rows at all
M1 remove the new check -> corrupt-side tests red, positives green; M2 revert the ldc widening instead -> the four positives red, so 'turn everything back into corrupt' is not a passing strategy
measurement trap: two worktrees sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR made cargo link a stale binary and report the opposite 'before'; caught with strings and a clean target dir
issues: One band stays open: LdcDynamicNoBSM answers 'unsupported' where OpenJDK says 'Missing BootstrapMethods attribute'. Bounding bootstrap_method_attr_index needs the attribute parsed, which belongs to the invokedynamic round. It is committed and asserted as it behaves today, so closing it will fail the assertion loudly.

The zero-cost measurement cannot exercise the >= 51 rows of the version table: every class in the 27,902-class corpus is major 69 or 70, and no class file older than Java 7 exists on this machine to test against.

The -fix round's own correction: the claim that 3,493 impossible operands bound the walker's error at 0.28% was wrong — that counts only *detectable* misdecodes, so it is an observation, not an upper bound. The conclusion survives because gate-② disassembled java.base independently with javap (7,401 classes, 92,659 ldc sites) and got zero.

The positive fixtures are synthetic. No javac construct emits ldc of these tags — measured over the JDK's own jmods, over targeted sources at --release 21/25/26+preview, and over this repo's test-data. No third-party jar corpus (where condy does occur) exists on this machine, so 'no bytecode generator in the wild does this either' was NOT measured.

The LdcUnknownTag/LdcTag13/LdcTag14 tests do not actually detect a pass-through constant-pool tag switch (M5); they pass for an adjacent reason. That axis is locked one layer down, by the previous round's classfile unit test.
Our runtime answers ClassFormatError where OpenJDK answers VerifyError for Ldc2WMethodType — we reject at parse time, earlier than the JVM's verification pass.

proposals.title: Bound bootstrap_method_attr_index against the BootstrapMethods attribute
proposals.plainSummary: A class file can name a bootstrap method that is not there. A real JVM refuses to read such a file; we still say we simply do not support the feature.
proposals.userBenefit: The one remaining case where a genuinely unreadable file is described as merely unsupported gets the right sentence.
proposals.why: The -fix round closed the other half of this (the tag-vs-class-file-version table) because that needs only ClassInfo.major_version. This half genuinely needs the BootstrapMethods attribute parsed, so it belongs with the invokedynamic work rather than here. JVMS 4.7.23 requires the attribute whenever the pool holds a Dynamic/InvokeDynamic entry, and requires the index to be in range; OpenJDK 26 enforces both ('Missing BootstrapMethods attribute'). test-data/ldc/LdcDynamicNoBSM.class is committed with an assertion pinning today's wrong answer, so this work will fail that test rather than land silently.
proposals.tradeoff: It is a behaviour change — files that parse today start being rejected — so it wants its own fixtures and its own cost measurement. It also cannot be done independently of the round that parses the attribute, which means sequencing, not just scope.

proposals.title: Make the constant-pool tag switch's pass-through mutation detectable end to end
proposals.plainSummary: A test that is supposed to prove 'we still reject unknown constant pool tags' does not actually prove it — it passes for a different reason.
proposals.userBenefit: None directly. It stops a future round from weakening the tag switch and believing a green test means the guard held.
proposals.why: M5 in this round: replacing the tag switch's reject arm with a pass-through left tests/test_class_format.rs entirely green. The end-to-end fixture passes because the mutation's hardcoded descriptor index fails a different validation rule, not because the tag was rejected. The axis is genuinely locked by constant_pool::tests::tags_outside_the_accepted_set_are_still_rejected, but a reader of the end-to-end test alone would draw the wrong conclusion.
proposals.tradeoff: Arguably nothing to fix: the unit test is the right layer for a parser-level rule, and duplicating it end to end is redundancy. The cheaper fix may be a comment on the end-to-end test naming which layer actually owns the axis — but that is a judgement, and this round did not make it.

proposals.title: Measure whether real-world bytecode generators emit ldc of tags 15/16/17
proposals.plainSummary: We proved javac never produces the class shape this round fixed. We could not check whether the tools that generate bytecode directly — ASM, Kotlin, Scala, Lombok — produce it.
proposals.userBenefit: It would say whether this round's fix is defensive-only or whether real jars on a user's classpath hit it, which changes how the invokedynamic work should be prioritised.
proposals.why: This round's corpus was the JDK's own jmods plus this repo's test-data: 28,029 classes, all javac output, zero hits. A find over $HOME, ~/.m2, ~/.gradle, ~/.ivy2, ~/Library/Caches and /opt/homebrew/Cellar returned zero jars, so the ASM/Kotlin side is simply unmeasured. Condy is known to be used by such generators; whether it reaches an ldc operand is the open question.
proposals.tradeoff: Needs jars this machine does not have, so it means downloading a corpus — which is an outbound fetch, and the round would have to be scoped to say what it may pull. Also a weak signal either way: 'some jar somewhere does it' does not by itself justify implementing condy. Low priority.
